text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Member of parliament Nicholas Biwott is the focus of parliamentary debate, with other members suggesting that he is heir apparent to President Daniel arap Moi following a cabinet reshuffle in January.
- Ethiopia accuses Kenya of violating its airspace after the deployment of Kenyan security patrols at the common border at the weekend.
- Kenyan judges and magistrates will not attend the East African Law Society's Annual General Meeting scheduled for Mbarara, Uganda on Friday. No explanation was given.
- A teacher from Nyasore Primary School in western Kenya is held by police as a nine-year-old pupil died after being beaten with a cane.
- Attorney General Amos Wako introduces a bill to parliament seeking to establish a National Crime Research Centre.
- President Moi challenges public universities to adopt business management strategies for greater efficiency and accountability.
- The Democratic Party of Kenya goes ahead with a proposed draft constitution that seeks to empower chairman Mwai Kibaki as the party's sole presidential candidate.
- The mode of distribution of the National Youth Development Fund will be made public before the end of next week.
- Police in the Mount Kenya district of Nyeri hold five villagers for lynching a man, hours after he had been acquitted of murder.
